title: What if you were stuck in an elevator for 24 hours?
style: Warm painterly 2D cartoon illustration, cinematic graphic-novel look: clean bold dark outlines, rich textured digital painting, soft volumetric light, deep warm oranges and moody blues, detailed environment, vertical 9:16 composition.
character: MAIN CHARACTER: a lanky ADULT man drawn as a minimalist cartoon: a perfectly round smooth tan head, two tiny solid black dot eyes set wide apart, short thin eyebrow strokes, a very small simple mouth, no nose, no visible hair, simple long limbs, dark charcoal baseball cap, oversized heather-grey hoodie, black slim pants, white sneakers. Minimal face like a webcomic, not a child, not anime, no big eyes.

scenes.A: Inside a small steel office elevator at night, the man stands alone, the lights flickering, holding a coffee cup, worried.

B.prompt: First-person point of view from the viewer's own eyes: no face, no head and no full body visible, only the viewer's own two cartoon hands in grey hoodie sleeves reaching in from the bottom of the frame. A finger presses a glowing red emergency call button on a steel elevator panel full of floor buttons, nothing happening.

scenes.C: The man sits on the floor of the dim elevator, back against the wall, emergency light glowing orange, backpack beside him.

D.prompt: First-person point of view from the viewer's own eyes: no face, no head and no full body visible, only the viewer's own two cartoon hands in grey hoodie sleeves reaching in from the bottom of the frame. The hands hold a half-empty plastic water bottle and a granola bar over a backpack on a steel elevator floor, dim orange light.

scenes.E: The man lies on the elevator floor using his hoodie as a pillow, sleeping, dim emergency light, quiet night.
scenes.F: The man knocks rhythmically on the steel elevator doors with his fist, determined, light from a crack between the doors.
scenes.G: Elevator doors pried open a few feet by a firefighter in a helmet, bright light flooding in, the man squinting with relief.
scenes.H: Close-up portrait of the man facing the viewer, tired relieved look, steel elevator walls behind him.

segments.text: The elevator stops between floors. It's Friday night. The building is empty.
You press the emergency button. Nothing.
Half a bottle of water. One granola bar. A thirty-one percent phone.
First rule: don't try to climb out. Elevators are built to hold you safely. The shaft isn't.
You sleep in shifts, and turn the phone off to save battery.
Then you hear footsteps. Monday's cleaning crew came in early.
You bang on the doors. Three knocks. Again. Again.
Twenty minutes later, the doors open.
Would you have stayed calm for twenty-four hours? Stick or twist?
